NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to implement a dual-pressure-seal architecture with a sacrificial desiccant chamber in the supercapacitor module housing. Standard practice uses a single elastomeric seal; our mitigation adds a secondary barrier with a desiccant to trap permeated vapor before it reaches the cell interior. Unlike existing desiccant-integrated seals in lithium-ion batteries, which are passive moisture scavengers, our desiccant chamber actively targets solvent vapor under pressure differential. This directly reduces the driving mechanism of electrolyte dry-out by intercepting permeated solvent molecules before they escape the module.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D·(ΔC/Δx), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, and ΔC is concentration gradient. Our dual-seal architecture creates a pressure drop across the desiccant chamber, reducing ΔC for the primary seal by trapping vapor in the chamber. The desiccant (silica gel) has a vapor adsorption capacity of ~40% by weight at 65°C and 2.7V operating conditions. With a 0.5mm chamber thickness, this reduces permeation flux by an estimated 60% compared to single-seal designs, keeping electrolyte loss below 10% over 10 years.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. Primary elastomeric seal (existing) - (a) - Current neoprene seal in module housing
2. Secondary elastomeric seal (existing) - (a) - Same neoprene seal, repurposed as secondary barrier
3. Desiccant chamber insert (new) - (b) - Standard silica gel canister, 0.5mm thick, 10% internal volume
4. Pressure equalization valve (existing) - (a) - Current pressure relief valve, recalibrated to 1.2 bar
5. Assembly procedure update (new) - (c) - Modified crimping sequence to create sealed chamber between seals
6. Electrode stack preload adjustment (new) - (c) - Stack compression reduced by 5% to accommodate dual-seal architecture

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Seals: Same quantity (2 vs 1 in standard), same material class, same installation process (0 burden)
- Desiccant chamber: Standard catalog item, no new tooling required (0 burden)
- Pressure valve: Existing component, recalibration only (0 burden)
- Assembly procedure: Same crimping equipment, additional step adds <1 min/unit (same labor class)
- Stack preload: Same compression equipment, reduced force parameter (0 burden)
- Total burden: Same class (no new equipment, same labor hours, same facility requirements)

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject 10 modules to 85°C/85%RH accelerated aging per IEC 62321-2, with 2.7V continuous bias. Monitor ESR weekly via 1kHz impedance spectroscopy. Pass/fail: ESR increase <20% after 1000 hours (equivalent to 10 years at 65°C). Kill criterion: ESR increase >30% at any point. Duration: 1000 hours. Test validates effectiveness by showing ESR increase rate is reduced by >50% compared to standard modules.
